grid.title: Charts like a spreadsheet
grid.blurb: Full-mouth Triadan grids for feline, canine, and deciduous dentition. One click to type, Tab/Enter/Space to fly through a called-out run of numbers.
grid.lead: The charting grid works the way your team already types: click any cell and go. Probing depths in, eyes on the patient.
grid.imageAlt: The charting grid with gingivitis, calculus, pocket, furcation and mobility values entered, and tooth 106 crossed out as missing

points.p1: Single click puts a cell straight into edit — no double-click dance.
points.p2: Tab, Enter, and Space advance exactly like a spreadsheet, so a called-out run ("3, 2, 4…") lands without looking.
points.p3: Whole-mouth scores in one action: set calculus or gingivitis for every tooth from the column header.
points.p4: The Missing checkbox crosses out the row and fills the tooth on the diagram — one source of truth.
points.p5: On a return visit, last time’s values appear as faint hints in empty cells: compare without opening the old chart.
points.p6: Feline, canine, puppy, and kitten dentitions, all Triadan-numbered.

voice.title: AI voice autofill, built in
voice.blurb: Say “104 complicated crown fracture” and it lands on the tooth — transcribed and charted while your hands stay on the patient.
voice.lead: Dictate as you work: a medical-grade speech model transcribes, and AI routes each finding onto the right tooth, diagram, and field.

points.p1: Medical-vocabulary speech recognition tuned with veterinary dental terms.
points.p2: Findings land as structured chart entries — grid values, tooth marks, anchored comments — not a wall of text.
points.p3: A live transcript sidebar shows every action as it happens; each one highlights the tooth it touched.
points.p4: Everything the AI writes goes through the same undo system as your own edits.
points.p5: Not sure it heard you right? It flags the finding and, after a pause, says “Check 109” in your ear — never over you.
points.p6: No API keys and no setup — free during the beta.

diagrams.title: Diagrams that stay in sync
diagrams.blurb: Diagnosis and procedure tooth diagrams follow the grid — cross a tooth out once and the whole record follows, chart to PDF.
diagrams.lead: Two anatomically-drawn diagrams — findings before, procedures after — that never disagree with the grid or the printed chart.
diagrams.imageAlt: The Diagnosis diagram with missing teeth filled in and AVDC codes — T/FX, T/FX/CCF, TR, AB, AT — anchored to each tooth

points.p1: Mark teeth missing or extracted with a click (or the keyboard — every tooth is focusable).
points.p2: Comments anchor to a tooth and stay pointed at it; free comments go anywhere.
points.p3: Freehand drawing in five colors for anything a code can’t say.
points.p4: Zoom and pan for crowded feline mouths.
points.p5: Teeth marked missing on Diagnosis lock on the Procedure diagram — you can’t re-extract what’s gone.
points.p6: Each diagram has its own undo stack (⌘Z follows whichever you touched last).

avdc.title: Speaks AVDC
avdc.blurb: The complete AVDC abbreviation set throughout, with a searchable reference beside the diagrams and a legend printed on every chart.
avdc.lead: The record reads cleanly in any hands: standard nomenclature end to end, and the reference is always one glance away.
avdc.imageAlt: The searchable AVDC code reference panel

points.p1: Complete AVDC abbreviation set for pathology and procedures.
points.p2: A searchable code reference sits beside each diagram — no separate tab, and it stays browsable even on locked charts.
points.p3: Every code used on the chart prints with its meaning in a legend on the PDF.
points.p4: Dental-code autocomplete in comment fields as you type.

pdf.title: Client-ready PDFs
pdf.blurb: A branded two-page chart the moment you finish — and the PDF itself can be re-imported later to restore the whole chart.
pdf.lead: One tap turns the chart into a polished document with your practice name, doctor line, and logo on it.
pdf.imageAlt: The generated canine dental chart PDF with diagrams, exam findings, and arch tables

points.p1: Two pages: diagrams, oral exam, full arch tables, treatment report, and the codes legend.
points.p2: Multiple document styles — pick per download, preview re-renders live.
points.p3: The chart’s full state is embedded in the PDF: re-import it later and keep working, even on another machine.
points.p4: Owner report (beta): a separate plain-English take-home version with before & after photos — auto-generated, editable before printing.

photos.title: Photos & radiographs
photos.blurb: Attach intraoral photos and dental rads to any chart, caption them, and pin each to a tooth — stored privately alongside the record.
photos.lead: The pictures live where you’ll look for them: on the chart, pinned to the tooth they show.

points.p1: Intraoral photos and radiographs, captioned and pinned per tooth.
points.p2: Private storage with short-lived signed links — images are never public.
points.p3: Phone photos are downscaled automatically so charts stay fast.
points.p4: Tag photos Before/After to drop them into the owner report (beta).

history.title: Every visit, one patient
history.blurb: Charts group by patient, so a returning animal’s whole history is one click away — and this visit starts where the last one ended.
history.lead: A patient is a story, not a pile of files. ToothOps keeps the visits together and carries the right things forward.

points.p1: Charts group by patient; a visit switcher in the topbar flips between dates.
points.p2: New visits carry extracted and missing teeth forward automatically — marked “prev” so they read as history, not today’s finding.
points.p3: Last visit’s measurements show as hints while you probe, so trends jump out chairside.
points.p4: Every save is logged — who, when — in each chart’s history.
points.p5: Past visits open read-only until deliberately unlocked, so records don’t change by accident — today’s visit stays ready to edit.

recall.title: Recall built in
recall.blurb: Set a recheck date as you chart; the patient list flags who’s due and who’s overdue, so the next dental never slips.
recall.lead: Recheck compliance is where dental outcomes are won — the list keeps score for you.

points.p1: A recheck date on the chart puts the patient on the Due list, flagged due or overdue.
points.p2: Send the owner a reminder email straight from the patient list.
points.p3: Recheck happened without a new chart? Clear it in one click and the patient drops off the list.
points.p4: Filter the library to due patients to plan the week’s callbacks.

team.title: Your whole team, one record
team.blurb: Add colleagues to your practice and everyone shares the same charts, templates, and images — per-person accounts, not a shared password.
team.lead: The practice is the unit: one shared record set, individual logins, and the doctor on each visit recorded.

points.p1: Up to five seats per practice (free during the beta); every member gets their own login.
points.p2: Charts, report templates, images, and the practice logo are shared automatically.
points.p3: Each visit records its author — filter the library by doctor.
points.p4: Owner-only controls for renaming the practice and managing the team.

offline.title: Cloud & chairside
offline.blurb: Every chart autosaves to the cloud and keeps a local copy chairside, so a dropped connection never loses a mouth.
offline.lead: Clinic Wi-Fi is not part of your anesthesia protocol. ToothOps assumes the connection will drop and plans around it.

points.p1: Every keystroke persists locally, instantly — a reload mid-procedure loses nothing.
points.p2: New charts autosave to the cloud; failed saves retry automatically when the connection returns.
points.p3: If your session expires mid-procedure, the chart stays open — sign back in right on top of it.
points.p4: Reusable report templates save the typing on every COHAT.
